argument: Found in Account and transaction activity risk indicators, page 8 (sub-bullets under pay-through/transit account). BA008 doctrine: 'funds already placed into the financial system are pushed through a chain of transfers designed to sever the audit trail... Intermediaries that are shell companies or nominee entities with no independent [purpose]... Cross-border routing through recognised secrecy or offshore jurisdictions... the seed amount split into multiple fragments across the chain.' The advisory describes a single incoming transfer being split and forwarded to multiple unrelated accounts, and cash routed onward to free-trade-zone/offshore parties with no business relationship -- the fragmentation-plus-offshore-routing mechanism BA008 names, which is distinct from the closed-loop pattern (BA004) and the intraday pass-through speed pattern (BA005) already claimed for this advisory.
doctrine_summary: Layering is the classic middle stage of money laundering: funds already placed into the financial system are pushed through a chain of transfers designed to sever the audit trail from their source before the proceeds are integrated into legitimate-looking assets. Unlike BA004 Circular Funds Flow (engineered to return to the originator), a layering chain has no obligation to close a loop — its only job is to put distance, opacity and jurisdictional friction between the seed account and wherever the funds end up.

evidence.quote: Incoming wire transfers to a trade-related account are split and forwarded to non-related multiple accounts that have little or no connection to commercial activity.

An account displays frequent deposits in cash which are subsequently transferred to persons or entities in free tra de zones or offshore jurisdictions without a business relationship to the account holder.

question: Should the ADV-2026-0002 label carry BA008 Layering?
